items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ralph Ellison, I remember him being very eloquent in what he talked about jazz

ctx.x: Eight pages long. It’s the transcription of what we had been playing all along. Okay, so he had somebody write this stuff out. Now, he said, “I just want to prove that black musicians can read music.” So, we were supposed to read this stuff on the television show. Now Lonnie Hillyer did not read music very well, and Charles McPherson did not read music very well, and this stuff was written out very technically. I mean, two eighth notes, how we would play it, he had it written out as we would play it. It was a…
When did you first record? Go into a recording studio?
